name: Thessaloniki
shape: Eurostat NUTS, the area it is named for

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Cabernet Sauvignon, Grenache, Carignan, Zinfandel and Nebbiolo fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Merlot is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Syrah is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen. Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 7°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
